results.summary_before: This project implements a current-based leaky integrate-and-fire neuron in Verilog. It accepts an 8-bit slice of input current on the switches, integrates it into a membrane potential that leaks over time, and emits a spike when the potential crosses a threshold. The membrane potential is shown on the 8 output pins and the spike on a bidirectional pin, with a 7-segment display mentioned for spike detection in the test description. The documentation is thin and the test instructions refer to hardware not fully described in the pin list, so external setup details are unclear.

results.summary_before: This is a test module for the TT05 power switching FET, featuring a ring oscillator and a 64-bit counter that counts oscillations. The counter value can be shifted and read on outputs, with reset and stop controls. It is tested by setting the shift value and observing the counter outputs. Silicon measurements indicated the ring oscillator runs at approximately 504 MHz, as inferred from a 1.969 MHz signal on the 8th counter bit.
results.summary: This project implements a 128-byte RAM module using a 32x32 1RW DFFRAM macro. It provides address, write-enable, input, and output pins for reading and writing data. The design is implemented in Verilog and spans a 4x2 tile area. Silicon test reports indicate that writes and reads work, with some timing quirks noted by testers.
